#### 1. What the user expresses

Target object, timing, boundary and authorisation are all clear from the script and need no inference:

- Object: *"you want to set up a standing monthly transfer from your checking into the money market account"*.
- Timing: *"You are quite clear that you want it set up today, on this call, and not just quoted."*
- Boundary: *"you want whatever the qualifying recurring amount is for your account, and you are happy for
  the representative to work it out"*; *"you would like it to run on the 5th of each month"*; *"you want it
  drawn from your Piedmont Crescent Bank checking account, not from anywhere else"*.
- Authorisation mode: the write is the owner's own. *"If the representative explains that the standing
  instruction is yours to give and hands the tool over to you, you go ahead and run it with the figure and
  the day they have given you... You do not run anything before it is handed to you, and you do not ask for
  it to be handed to you."*

The simulator is passive throughout: it conveys the need, releases identifiers one at a time on request
(mobile `3365550247`, then DOB `1969-03-22`, SSN last four `1246`, ZIP `27410`), never names an amount,
never proposes a next step, and executes the user-owned tool only after the agent hands it over. On the
prerequisite work it says only *"that is fine and to go ahead and do whatever they need to - you trust them
with it, and you do not ask what it is for or what it comes to"* — i.e. it supplies **no** information that
would identify the prerequisites. They must be derived from the KB and the records.

#### 3. Narrowest business object, keys, rows in / out

- Object: the single Money Market Account `ab0c9bef…6317`; the single Interest Checking `da40a004…8823` as
  funding account and as the Personal Checking relationship read by three factors.
- Keys: `customer_id` → `savings_account_id` / `checking_account_id` / `card_account_id` /
  `certificate_id`; `savings_txn_id` ↔ `source_item_id` for fee-to-item links.
- Ledger rows in scope are the 29 rows of `find_savings_transactions(savings_account_id=ab0c9bef…)`.
- **Window convention used.** The corpus writes every measurement window as "the *N* calendar months ending
  on the review/correction/instruction date". Read as a calendar-month-length span anchored on that date —
  the same sense the corpus uses elsewhere for "calendar months" (*Dormancy…*: "once the tier's dormancy
  period in calendar months has passed after the last customer-initiated activity"; *Opening…*: "the opening
  date plus the tier's promotional duration in calendar months"). The alternative reading (month-to-date from
  the 1st) is excluded because *Basis of the Courtesy Credit* says the pool is "**the** monthly maintenance
  fee posted … in the one calendar month ending on the review date" in the singular, and *Width of the
  Refundable Fee Pool* prices its worked case at one maintenance fee per one-calendar-month window and three
  per three-calendar-month window; month-to-date on 16 September would capture none. **Recorded as a
  residual risk**: the corpus never states which endpoint day the window opens on, unlike the funding,
  early-closure and courtesy windows, each of which says "the day after … as day 1". No row in this task sits
  on that boundary, so the answer is unaffected.
  - one calendar month ending 2026-09-16 ≈ 2026-08-17 … 2026-09-16
  - three calendar months ≈ 2026-06-17 … 2026-09-16
  - twelve calendar months ≈ 2025-09-17 … 2026-09-16
- Row counts taken from the ledger (excluded rows named): deposits 3 in the 3-month window
  (07-10 4000.00 ach_credit, 08-05 6500.00 check_deposit, 09-04 2800.00 ach_credit; the 04-20 30000.00
  opening deposit is out of window); withdrawals 3 in the 3-month window (07-22 3900.00 online_transfer,
  08-19 6200.00 ach_debit, 09-11 2650.00 online_transfer; 05-06 and 06-03 internal transfers are out of
  window); fee entries 6 in the 3-month window (06-28, 07-28, 08-28 each a 12.00 monthly_maintenance and a
  2.00 paper_statement); interest entries 8 in the 3-month window; withdrawals 5 and deposits 4 in the
  12-month window; fee entries 8 in the 12-month window.

#### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The customer named **one** problem: set up a standing monthly transfer. Four problems are required.

```
  [P4] promotional interest correction (agent)
        └─ blocks ─>
  [P3] relationship bonus correction (agent)
        └─ blocks ─>                        [P2] courtesy credit for periodic fees (agent)
                     \                     /
                      └─ both block ─> [P1] standing monthly transfer (customer's own write)
```

Handling order: **P4 → P3 → P2 → P1** (P2 may be taken anywhere before P1).

**Hop 1 — P1 waits on P3.** *Recording a Standing Monthly Transfer into a Savings or Money Market Account*
(the hub of the problem the customer raised) states: *"The qualifying recurring amount is worked out only
after the account's posted balance carries the relationship bonus owed for every closed statement cycle."*
This names a **record-visible state** — the posted balance carrying the bonus owed — not an action.
`find_savings_transactions` shows the last relationship-bonus interest credit posted 2026-08-28 for cycle
`2026-08`; that cycle is closed and, worked through the settlement basis below, 4.23 USD of it is still
unpaid, so the state does not hold. Searching the records' own words for that state ("relationship bonus
owed closed statement cycle") returns *Settlement Basis for Relationship Bonus Owed on a Closed Statement
Cycle* and *Crediting Relationship Bonus Left Unpaid by a Closed Statement Cycle*; the latter describes the
write that brings the state about: *"Where relationship bonus interest stands owed … for a statement cycle
that has already closed, that bonus is settled on the account as a correction to that cycle."*
→ **state-derived**.

**Hop 2 — P3 waits on P4.** *Settlement Basis for Relationship Bonus…* states: *"The relationship bonus
owed for a closed statement cycle is settled only after the promotional interest due on that cycle's new
money stands credited on the account."* Again a record-visible state. The ledger's promotional interest
entries stop at 1.85 on 2026-08-28, and the settlement basis for the 2026-08 cycle yields 9.50 still owed,
so the state does not hold. The words of the state ("promotional interest … closed statement cycle") lead to
*Settlement of Promotional Interest Owed on a Closed Statement Cycle* and to *Crediting Promotional Interest
Left Unpaid by a Closed Statement Cycle*, which describes the write: *"Where promotional interest stands
owed … for a statement cycle that has already closed, that promotional interest is settled on the account as
a correction to that cycle."* → **state-derived**.

**Hop 3 — P1 waits on P2.** *Working Out the Qualifying Recurring Amount for a Standing Monthly Transfer*
(a fragment of the problem the customer raised) states: *"Before the qualifying recurring amount is fixed,
the courtesy credit owed against the periodic fees standing on the account must already appear in its posted
balance."* A record-visible state. The ledger carries three 12.00 monthly maintenance fees and five 2.00
paper statement fees and **no** `savings_fee_refund` row at all, so no courtesy credit appears in the posted
balance. The words of the state ("courtesy credit … periodic fees") lead to *Basis of the Courtesy Credit
for Periodic Savings Account Fees* and to *Courtesy Credit for Periodic Fees Standing on a Savings Account*,
which describes the write: *"Where periodic fees stand on an account … and a courtesy credit is due against
them, that credit is put back onto the account as one courtesy refund entry."* → **state-derived**.

**No hop was pre-solved.** Each of the three prerequisite sentences names a state and nothing else: no tool
name, no policy id, no route, no "call X first". Verified mechanically — each of the six task-tool names
occurs in exactly one document, its own hub (`grep -o -E '\`[a-z_]+_[0-9a-f]{8}\`'` over the 68 files gives
one occurrence each, in `standing_transfer_instruction_service`, `relationship_bonus_correction_service`,
`promotional_interest_correction_service`, `periodic_fee_courtesy_credit_service`,
`excess_withdrawal_fee_review_service`, `surplus_transfer_instruction_service` respectively). No document
lists the chain, and no document mentions more than one of the four problems' writes.

#### 7. Two-way counter-proof

**(a) The visible materials fully support the conclusion, and the closest alternatives are excluded.**

- *Closest alternative starting point in time.* Could the corrections belong to cycle `2026-09` rather than
  `2026-08`? Excluded: the service documents say the cycle is "the month in which that cycle **closed**",
  and `statement_cycle_day=28` with today 2026-09-16 puts the September cycle still open (it closes
  2026-09-28). The last closed cycle is 2026-08.
- *Closest alternative object set.* Could the reviewable/refundable pool reach into other accounts? Excluded:
  `find_savings_accounts(customer_id=…)` returns exactly one savings account, and every pool in the corpus is
  defined "posted to the account".
- *Closest alternative discount combination.* Could the promotional uplift be 0.25 pp rather than 0.60?
  Excluded by the count: *Card-Linked Uplift* puts "4 or more" in the 0.60 band and there are exactly 4 card
  purchases in the 3-month window; *"A count of exactly 4 card purchases falls in the first band."*
  Could the bonus rate lift be 0.35 rather than 0.85? Excluded: *"A ledger balance of exactly 6000.00 USD
  takes the 0.85 percentage point lift"*, and 8450.00 is above it.
- *Closest alternative ordering.* Could the courtesy credit be taken after the standing transfer? Excluded:
  the prerequisite sentence is "Before the qualifying recurring amount is fixed … must already appear in its
  posted balance."
- *Closest alternative business action.* Could the agent set the standing transfer itself? Excluded:
  *"It is the customer's own tool: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs
  it."* And `query.py … tools agent` confirms `set_savings_standing_transfer_55216172` is not on the agent's
  surface; only `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` reaches it.
- *Where the source leaves a boundary open, the documents leave it open too.* The window-endpoint day and the
  rounding-vs-truncation of "kept to four decimal places" are both open on the visible surface; neither is
  closed by any document, and neither changes this task's answer (§3 and §4(d)). Recorded as openness, not as
  a document defect.

**(b) Excluding the natural wrong answer "do only the one thing the customer asked for".**
Setting the standing transfer straight away is excluded by reasoning, not by any route statement. The
qualifying recurring amount is defined off the account's **posted balance**
(*"The posted balance is the total of the deposits, interest credits and fee refunds posted to the account
less the withdrawals and fees posted to it"*). Two visible sentences forbid fixing that amount while the
balance is short of what is owed: the courtesy credit *"must already appear in its posted balance"* and the
amount *"is worked out only after the account's posted balance carries the relationship bonus owed for every
closed statement cycle"*. The records show neither condition holds (no fee-refund row at all; relationship
bonus entries stop at 2026-08-28 with 4.23 still owed for that closed cycle). So the one-step answer fixes
the amount on a balance of 1823.78 rather than 1878.51: shortfall 926.22, less the 400.00 deposit offset =
526.22, halved over the 2-month spread = 263.11, paced at 1.25 = 328.8875, rounded to 329.00 USD instead of
295.00 — a state the visible principles do not allow. The exclusion runs entirely through state sentences plus the ledger; no
document had to tell the solver which tool to call.

**(c) The fall-back number for each computation is definite, and differs from the answer reached.**
Reading only the computation document plus the product figures it names, with no factor applied:

| computation | baseline-only value | value reached | factor documents actually used |
|---|---|---|---|
| promotional interest correction | new money 13300.00 − offset 12750.00 = 550.00 basis; 550.00 × 3.50 ÷ 100 × 31 ÷ 365 = 1.6349 → half up to the cent 1.63; less promotional interest credited in the one-month window 1.85 → **0.00** (never less than zero) | **9.50** | counting window, withdrawals offset, card uplift, accrual span, rounding, credits already paid |
| relationship bonus correction | ledger basis 1879.28 less withdrawals in the 3-month window 12750.00 → 0.00 after the floor; 0.00 × 0.15 × 31 ÷ 365 = 0.00; less 0.27 → **0.00** | **4.23** | further reduction, review span, day count, rate lift, credits already deducted |
| courtesy credit | pool = the one maintenance fee in the one-month window 12.00; × 0.50 = 6.00 → half up to the cent 6.00; allowance amount (2 − 0) × 12.00 = 24.00; ceiling 24.00 → lesser = **6.00** | **41.00** | pool width, allowance count, goodwill share, rounding, binding ceiling |

**(d) How each factor document was reached from the customer's records.** In each case the words are the
records' own, not the computation document's:

- *Counting Window for Qualifying New Money* — from the checking account's `checking_deposit` rows of
  channel `ach_direct_deposit` ("direct deposits credited to the owner's Personal Checking account").
- *Offsetting Window Withdrawals Against Qualifying New Money* — from `find_cd_certificates` showing a
  `principal_balance` of 18500.00 ("certificate under Certificates of Deposit", "principal").
- *Card-Linked Uplift*, *Spread Period*, *Width of the Refundable Fee Pool*, *Further Reduction … by Card
  Standing* — from the card account's `card_purchase` / `card_payment` rows, `current_balance` and
  `rewards_balance` ("card purchases", "card payments", "balance owed", "unredeemed rewards points").
- *Accrual Span*, *Bonus Review Span*, *Goodwill Share*, *Share of the Surplus*, *Rounding of the Instalment*
  — from `opened_date` on the savings account and the deposit/fee rows ("whole months the account has been
  open", "deposits posted", "fee entries posted").
- *Balance Target Cushion*, *Lift to the Relationship Bonus Rate* — from the checking account's
  `ledger_balance` and its direct-deposit rows.
- *Courtesy Allowance Count* — from `variant_name='Interest Checking'` on the checking account and the
  absence of a recent `checking_fee_refund`. **Findability note (not a computed-number defect):** the savings
  factor asks for "how many **courtesy** fee refunds in a rolling 365 days the owner's checking tier allows",
  while the Personal Checking schedule prices the same parameter as "**Goodwill** refunds allowed in any
  rolling 365 days". The bridge is the tier name, which the factor does name along with the product; the
  value was found, but through the tier rather than through the term.
- *Standing Transfer Ceiling*, *Pacing Adjustment*, *Setting Recently Deposited Money…*, *Binding Ceiling*,
  *Rounding of the Courtesy Credit*, *Rounding of Promotional Interest*, *Day Count Convention*, *Credits
  Already Paid/Deducted* — from the savings ledger's own withdrawal, deposit, fee and interest rows.

No factor document announces its own existence from the computation document: none of the four baselines
says "unless otherwise provided", "adjustments may apply" or points anywhere. Each factor was found because a
record showed a card, a certificate, a checking relationship or an age — which is the intended discovery path.

source layer's solution, including the three hops of a problem tree the customer never mentioned, all four

where the source writes, no two equally reasonable formulas or object sets were found, no conclusion rested
